extracted.intended_audience: clinically trained investigators (physician-scientists and other clinician-researchers) applying for the NINDS K08 Mentored Clinical Scientist Research Career Development Award
extracted.subtask_short: NINDS K08 mentored career award application
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting an application for the NINDS K08 Mentored Clinical Scientist Research Career Development Award, including eligibility, effort, institutional commitment, budget limits, and career-development expectations. Focused on clinician-scientists seeking mentored research training to become independent investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose / career development objective
rubrics_metrics.description: The mentored K awards for clinicians (K08, K23) is to provide scholars with the skills, education and protected time that will enable them to launch an independent research career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award is designed to provide 'protected time' for clinically trained individuals to receive intensive, supervised research training in biomedical research related to neurological disorders and to prepare the candidate to successfully obtain an NIH R01 or equivalent major research award by the end of the K award period. Applicants should represent that 4–5 years of additional mentored training is required to achieve independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project originality and candidate ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: The importance of project originality and project ownership by the candidate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate that the candidate owns the proposed research and that the project is original; see linked document 'The importance of project originality and project ownership by the candidate' for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional commitment / Letter of Institutional Commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific issues must be addressed in a statement of institutional support for K08 awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Letter of Institutional Commitment must include critical information (see 'Information on institutional commitment' PDF). Applicants should pay careful attention to what MUST be provided in that letter for an award to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career development plan quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must present a strong career development plan that provides supervised research training and prepares the candidate for independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'Suggestions for a Good Career Development Plan' for guidance; the plan should describe training, mentoring, coursework, timelines, and how the award will enable competitiveness for an R01 or equivalent by award end.

rubrics_metrics.name: PD/PI eligibility (clinical licensure and degrees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research and/or clinical doctorate holders that are licensed to practice clinically are eligible to be PD/PI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award is primarily targeted to candidates holding an MD or equivalent degree, but will also support other health professional degrees. Applicants must be licensed to practice clinically in the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship / immigration eligibility at time of award
rubrics_metrics.description: By the time of award, applicants must be U.S. Citizens or permanent residents (i.e. possess a valid 'green card').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-citizens without permanent residency are not eligible to receive the award at the time it would be activated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-training timing constraint / prior approval for >5 years post-training
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants that are beyond 5 years post clinical training must obtain prior approval from the Office of Training & Workforce Development to be eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-residency and clinical fellowship training are counted; if more than five years have elapsed, secure prior approval before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effort requirement (non-neurosurgeons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for neurosurgeons, candidates must devote a minimum of 75% full time professional effort to the proposed research and career development activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a minimum commitment expected for the duration of the K award; institutional commitment letters should reflect and support this protected effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effort requirement (neurosurgeons)
rubrics_metrics.description: NINDS will accept 50% full time professional effort for research and career development activities associated with the K award for neurosurgeons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neurosurgeon applicants are allowed this lower effort percentage; institutional commitment documentation should still clearly reflect the protected effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award duration (length of K08 support)
rubrics_metrics.description: NINDS mentored K awards may be for either 4 or 5 years (NINDS will not make K08 awards lasting only 3 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must represent a need for 4–5 years of mentored training in their application; plan timelines accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary support cap
rubrics_metrics.description: NINDS will provide up to $125,000 salary, plus appropriate fringe, per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy applies to new (Type 1) applications submitted on or after Feb 12, 2016, and non-competing continuations with appropriate start dates; budget the application consistent with this cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research (program) support cap
rubrics_metrics.description: NINDS will provide up to $51,000 per year for research support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NOT-NS-13-028 for additional details and permitted uses of the research support (research development costs, supplies, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior institutional K support and total mentored K limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may request up to 5 years of K08 funding subsequent to up to 3 years of prior institutional K (e.g., K12, KL2) support; thus applicants to NINDS may receive up to a maximum of 8 years of mentored K support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants previously supported on an institutional K must clearly explain in their application the career development needs that justify additional mentored K support. Consider K02 for investigators approaching independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent submission / award policy (R01 vs mentored K)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should not submit an R01 application simultaneously with a mentored K application (or similarly, have one of each pending simultaneously).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mentored K application represents that additional mentored training is required; an R01 application represents independence. After receiving a mentored K award, one may apply for and receive an R01 and keep both awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate funding opportunity depends on human subjects/clinical trial status
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants with human subjects must determine whether their research qualifies as a clinical trial or as a basic experimental study with humans and choose the appropriate funding opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are strongly advised to consult with NINDS program staff prior to submitting an application with human subjects to determine the appropriate funding opportunity; see NIH definition of a clinical trial and NIH guidance for basic experimental studies with humans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission due dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Due Dates for New/Resubmission Applications: February/March 12, June/July 12, October/November 12.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must be submitted on the applicable receipt dates for new or resubmission applications; plan timelines to meet institutional routing and these deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy encouraging early applicants with strong pre-residency records
rubrics_metrics.description: NINDS encourages clinicians with excellent pre-residency research publication records to apply for a K08 without waiting for post-residency publications (NOT-NS-15-048).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong pre-residency research productivity may justify applying earlier in training; consult the policy notice for details.
